reviews.review_text: My husband and I enjoy trying local cuisine and new experiences with dining options. Well this place is certainly one of those places. The ambience is great for a couple or small group in this quaint setting. The experience will be unforgettable for sure!!

reviews.review_text: We had a excellent lunch experience. After eating two tasting menus in a row, we switched to à la cart in the morning. We are super grateful for that. We’re also thankful that the staff was so easy to accommodate us. The à la carte menu has a lot of different options. The waitress was able to make recommendations on what we should order. The scallops with sankey is definitely a must have. I probably could’ve eaten another couple of those. It was so light and refreshing. The Popeye crab was also very interesting with almost thai flavors, very balanced. The fish curry was cooked perfectly. The different flavors mixed with the pani puri bread was super fun. The rice with squid was also very well thought out. The fresh peas added the texture that it needed. It was a homey and very thoughtful dish. Thankfully, we received room for dessert. The flan is the best flan I’ve ever had in my entire life. The custard was luxurious and luscious on the tongue. Definitely a highlight. The grilled custard apple with such an interesting dish. It was fun to eat and had a great almost pancake toast on the bottom, topped with a grilled custard, apple, topped with a crisp of the custard apple. On the side, there was almost this goat cheese/funky ice cream, which really complimented everything. It was by far one of the most interesting and flavorful dishes.

Flavors were out of this world and the combinations of food, flavor, and texture was outstanding.  We also did the South American wine pairing which was the perfect compliment to every course.  Staff were the ultimate professionals.  This in itself would have made for the most memorable night on our trip, but when we struggled to catch an uber due to no international cell service plus construction in the area Chef Martinez himself came out to help us, walked 2 blocks with us, and only left once we got into the car.  So not only is he one of the best chefs in the world but a kind and helpful man at his core.  If you travel to Lima your trip will not be complete without a stop at Merito.

Each dish had a constant, this acidity foretold so much that, at the end of the ten courses, it was all so obvious in taste that boredom had taken over. Every single dish ended with this sour tone and all this was repeated again and again. 

Atmosphere: Medium/high music and very loud cold air conditioning made the room uncomfortable. Beautiful lighting. 

Service: our table was tied, for service, to another table, so, if we had not yet finished the other table had to wait and vice versa. In addition, we were served by 4 different waiters who could not explain the ingredients used (except superficially) while the explanation of the ingredients was supposed to be the main focus of this experience. 

Disappointment is so much also because it seems to enter a temple of cuisine and everything tries to be so perfect that then at the end of dinner you do not have much left except, precisely, this immense disappointment. The price is high, the disappointment more!

reviews.review_text:
This was bought as a 40th wedding anniversary gift by our 3 adult kids as they knew that we were coming to Peru and our son had eaten there a few years before.
The building is unusual in that you walk through the kitchen with a chefs table and taken upstairs to the restaurant itself. It does have the industrial vibe with bare bricks etc but our table and chairs were comfortable. We were having the 10 course tasting menu and the staff were very attentive to my allergen request of no onions. 
Each course was fantastic with Peruvian ingredients the majority we had never heard of. The flavours were amazing as well as having playful variations in texture and colours. Each course was explained by the staff with advice how to eat it to get the most out of each course.
By the sixth course I was feeling full and was worrying whether I would be able to finish the menu but the chef’s playfulness came into its own and I finished the meal just right.
We had a bottle of Albariño which complemented the food. 

The meal was simply stunning on all levels and entered my top 10 meals eaten out and we have eaten in quite a few Michelin star restaurants including Arzak, Gordon Ramseys and L’Enclume and is was as good as them.

Sat near us was an American guy sat by himself having the same menu taking photos.
We met him outside and had a quick chat about the meal. He had visited a  world renowned restaurant around the corner and said this meal was one third of the price and twice as good- I think that summed up the whole experience for us.
reviews.title: Fantastic, amazing, sensational….I could go on.

reviews.review_text:
We had looked forward to our trip to Merito for several months and once we’d arrived in Peru , our anticipation grew as we found the incredible level of respect found across the whole country for ingredients. Peru is not known as the garden of South America for nothing, with the variety of ecosystems that support multitudes of flora & fauna.

 Chef Juan Luis Martinez, graciously allowed us to take our tasting menu at the bar in the kitchen and watching the team at work in their creation of the dishes that we were to consume was a fantastic experience. A menu that takes modern and classic cooking techniques with a laser like focus on ingredients. You’re hard put to find a superfluous ingredient on a plate here. Everything has a place and a reason for its inclusion.

We both took the tasting menu, a representation of around 10 courses that take you on a journey inspired both by the chef’s Venezuelan heritage in addition to the Peruvian backscape of ingredients available. The Coast, the Amazon & The Andes provided Swordfish. Crab, Scallops and Lobster, Paiche ( a large freshwater fish) and young Goat for us together with a selection of tubers, quinoas and vegetables some of which I had never come across previously, to create a menu which  represented the best of Peru & Venezuela  in both technique and combination. The light smoke given to most dishes by virtue of the carob tree wood glowing in the oven gave a light but intense addition to dishes which was well received. I also took the Wine pairing to accompany the menu, a voyage which took us all over South America from Peru to Uruguay to Argentina & Chile with wines that were challenging but never to the point of disrupting the balance and harmony with their accompanying dishes. Often small or even micro producers. The wine pairing had obviously been considered at length and much like the menu everything had a reason & rationale for being there.

This was an epic journey and whilst one might easily think that this was entirely led by the dishes presented. Our waiter with his intimate knowledge of the dishes meant that rather than just reeling off a list of ingredients (as is often found in good restaurants) we were given deep descriptions of cooking techniques, sourcing of ingredients and more which gave a significantly deeper understanding and thus enjoyment of everything we ate. Supplemented by the Sommeliers previously noted excellent wine choices and informative descriptions, made for a more than excellent evening. Merito provides excellent value for a restaurant of its calibre but do not mistake value for any loss of quality. From someone who has been fortunate enough to visit a significant number of Michelin starred and highly rated restaurants, The gastronomic journey to be found at Merito is one of the best!
reviews.title: Sensational dinner!!

What a great experience! We were visiting Lima for a few days  post a tour of Peru! We love good food. We were not disappointed. The restaurant is located in the trendy area, Barranco. The restaurant is humble and minimalist in its decor with a ‘cool’ relaxing vibe. The staff greeted us warmly and were super helpful about the menu and drinks. We had the following and loved everything:

Pez & Kiwicha
Mamet & Cangrejo popeye
Conchas, Sandi & Jalapeño
Choclo al la brasa
Cabrita & Tuberculos
El Flan
Roca 

The quality and presentation was high and the incredible flavour combinations. The recommended wine by the sommelier was perfect. (Vigo carignan). So glad we could visit. Highly recommended.

reviews.review_text: We were lucky to get a seat at the bar without a reservation. The bar seats were not super comfortable but the service, food and atmosphere were so good that we didn't care all that much. The drink service was interesting with unusual and well-crafted cocktails and a nice selection of wines. There were also interesting non-alcoholic drinks. We had two appetizers, one was a remarkable concoction with different types of corn that was incredibly complex and delicious, the other was scallops with sanki and jalapeno that were super fresh and perfect. We had pork belly, perfectly cooked and served with puffy arepas to stuff it into along with a couple of sauces and lightly pickled cabbage. and we had the fish of the day; a pacific white fish that was perfectly cooked and came with a delicious Peruvian black mint sauce. The chocolate rock and the, if I remeber correctly, Cherimoya cherimoya cherimoya - three varieties of dessert featuring the fruit, were both superb. I'm not sure how much good knowing what we ate will do you; the menu changes frequently. I am looking forward to going back.
reviews.title: Great interesting restaurant with local ingredients.

reviews.review_text:
The positives:
The room is lovely, with a bit of an industrial vibe. 
The food is beautiful presented. 
Service is attentive.

The not so good:
The air con fans spew very cold air on your neck, suffered from a headache the entire day after (no, I didn’t drink too much). 
Some of the sauces with the main courses are way too salty. At a certain point I couldn’t even taste the nuances of the dishes, all I could taste was salt. 
No real vegetables in the dishes. 
Reading the menu it’s a bit hard to gauge how large the portions may be, making it difficult to know how much to order. 
A couple of dishes weren’t described properly by the server, ended up ordering a frozen dessert concoction when I was already cold, just because the words “cold” or “frozen” were never used.

reviews.review_text:
My husband and I visited Merito for a lunch date.

It was the last of the top 50 restaurants in the world located in Lima we were yet to try and expectations were high.

The restaurant is located in a traditional shop in Barranco, just around the corner from Central and Kjolle.

The entrance is through the open kitchen and then you get promptly taken to the table upstairs.

There are two rooms with 6 tables each (quite close to each other). The style is smart casual and the crowd is very trendy.

We opted for a selection of dishes which we shared, accompanied by wine (there is no matching, you pick wine by glass or go for a bottle).

We thought that Scallops, sanki and jalapeños & white fish with cocoa fruit were good,  octopus, fish curry and arepas were fantastic and so was flan (one of the best I’ve ever had). Coconut dessert was average and so was the wine selection by glass.

Overall we had a nice afternoon, ate well and thought it was value for money (£170 for two, including 3 glasses of wine each & teas and coffees)

reviews.review_text: * Merit - located in the “young” neighborhood called “barrancas” the merit offers a tapas style menu. Small dishes to divide. We ordered the corn, the popai crab, and the entrance caterpillars. Tasty, but nothing spectacular. The crab, in particular, had a strange taste. The best are the main dishes, highlighting the pork and the curry’ fish that were great. It is among the 7 best in Latin America according to expert critics. Price below the average of the others. It is worth going there and dps go pro bar Ayuhasca, which is in the same neighborhood. Ps: bons drinks

reviews.review_text:
I loved everything about our dinner at Merito. The ambiance and music are relaxed and chic, and my husband and I were blown away by the food. 

The crackers with Andean grains and white fish and the seafood curry were outstanding, and we had a ceviche with a fruit we've never tried before that was excellent. If you are a pescatarian or a fan of fresh fish you must try Merito! The value is also excellent-we didn't pay much more than we would for a standard dinner out in NYC and everything about our experience was exceptional. 

I had an excellent cocktail with coconut and cardamom. The N/A cocktail options were also sophisticated and the one my husband ordered was delicious. 

The service is also top-notch. Alexandra was especially helpful and patient answering our many questions and gently offering recommendations. 

Even among the countless excellent dining options in Lima I would absolutely go back to Merito, and I will be dreaming out it until then!

reviews.review_text:
We went out of the way to Barranco for a dinner at Mérito and it did not disappoint.

We had two main dishes, "oyster mushroom rice with asparragus and Andesino pesto", and "glazed pork belly with arepas". The rice dish was very good. The pork with arepas (corn dough stuffed with meat) was a bit cultue shock to me as a Chinese. We have something similar called roujiamo back at home. The pork belly was delicious, but I find it a bit difficult to eat it that way.

The dessert "corn and coffee cloud with lucuma and macambo" was very creative and delicious.

Service was a bit hit and miss. One gentleman was very nice. He explained the dishes very well and answered all my questions. Some other staff members were not proactive at all. I would expect better service for a restaurant ranked at 59 in the world.

We spent around US$30 per person, without any drinks. It was not cheap for Peru, but very reasonable compared to similar food back at home.
reviews.title: Good food at a reasonable price

reviews.review_text:
After 1 1/2 hours we had received one single starter, which was not harmonic in taste.

We were HUNGRY, asked when the other dishes should come. The waiter said ‚when they come, they come‘. Since the guests next table told us they were sitting already since 2 1/2 hours we asked for the bill.

When leaving we informed the owner why we‘re leaving and he just said ‚ok‘, no excuse, no explanation.

This restaurant is living for its previous reputation, the owner is trying to squeeze out of his reputation as much as he can.

reviews.review_text:
If I could rate this restaurant with more than 5 stars, I would! A small, stylish and utterly delightful restaurant located in the upmarket area of Barranco. Reservations a must to secure a booking. The Chef Patron, Juan Luis Martinez and the team underneath him are geniuses. The restaurant is ranked 11th in South America and 59th in the world. Would not surprise me if it pushes even higher. 

Service is second to none - thoroughly professional, superbly trained and knowledgeable, polite and friendly. 

As for the food… I can describe this in one word: sublime! But I will use more. This restaurant provides a deep dive into Peruvian and South American cuisine, taking local dishes and elevating them to fine dining. Moreish and enlightening your taste buds. Devine. Memorable. Outstanding. 

We were just wowed. This sits there as one of the best restaurants we have ever eaten at. This is a perfect example of how food and service should be delivered. Bravo!

reviews.review_text:
We chose the 8 pm shift and I arrived before my wife. I stood outside until a waiter came out and asked: have they opened, YES are we already open? It was then that a woman came out asking if I had a reservation, I gave her the information and passed.
I greeted 10 people who were in the kitchen with a kind and necessary good night and only ONE person answered. I imagine the concentration when preparing your dishes required that degree of absence from external reality, so I got excited and thought: what good dishes await us.
Luis served us, very friendly and descriptive with the dishes, but he had no idea which dish to serve and/or offer first, which we paid for with a mix of hot and cold dishes that left a lot to miss, longing for Merito from when it wasn't award-winning that it was when we went up to 3 times and we always liked it. This time it was not the case. I don't know if the main chef is so worried about this recognition that he forgot the essential thing about his food: the flavor! and replaced it with the presentation. Thank you but we hope not to return soon
reviews.title: 'Disappointment after recognition

For example, their pork dish basically tasted like a pork bun (except this had arepas) that you could get in many Chinese restaurants in NY. Their fish was a bit over cooked so it had a rubbery texture.

reviews.review_text:
From passionatepalate

Meager Zen

Lima is a sprawling metropolis with an industrious twelve million of population blessed with a trading gene. Each Peruvian gives the impression of trying with diverse selling maneuvers and products to progress in the pursuit of attaining the next level within the orbit and hierarchy of enterprise. Lima is a zoo of traffic congested enthusiasts decidedly in formula one training.

Merito, this somewhat compressed diner, with a nondescript easily ignored façade is readily mimicked within as you penetrate directly into the kitchen. The first glance is the portrait of the seven cooking recruits all intent in the sublimation and brewing of the elements. You are spellbound witnessing the activity and shuffle of the ingredients. Merely the delicate scent of the spices becomes the catalyst that stirs the anticipation of feasting

Joan, the student of physics awaiting the doctorate, is temporarily director of alignment who accompanies you up the staircase to your dining abode. The decor is composed of sleek wooden surfaces that gently embraces you as you gaze at the starving Zen ambience which surrounds you. The atmosphere is set to calm.

The menu composition is either oceanic ( catch of the day) or meat-based (Beef cheeks or glazed pork belly).

We opted for the ocean sea bass curry style and fish accompanied by potato noodles.

The presentation of both dishes is obviously caressed by artistic input. The result is mesmerizing and the flaky flesh of fish bathing in a chili cream sauce imparts its delightful picante absolved of its picante with only residual flavor.  

The pastries are home grown with the similar artististic input that brags the external appearance of each dainty and soothes and sighs on ingestion. On the whole I am not the first nor the last to state the obvious: outstanding

This fine discovery is on a trajectory of testing new summits

Jean-Louis Bourque, Montreal, Quebec, Canada
reviews.title: Meager Zen

reviews.review_text: We booked here on a recommendation and based on reviews. It is rather overrated and seems to benefit from hype. The main courses are nothing special - they are not at all balanced. They are also very small and therefore overpriced. They were described as 'personal', but are more like small starters or tapas, though priced as a main. One was two small pieces of meat with two sauces and a scattering of tiny crisps. There was no vegetables or sufficient carbohydrates. No no side dishes are offered to create a more full meal. A choice of these should be offered within the price of each plate. The second main was too salty. Desserts were better; tasty and nicely presented, they offered slightly better value for money. Alcoholic drinks were too expensive and small. The menu does not sufficiently explain what any dish is, or what it comes with. One was simply translated as 'coconut'. The glowing reviews about incredible food just do not match what we encountered - it is perhaps more about saying you have been than it actually being fantastic. Overall, it is trying too hard and has a few too many gimmicks when good, balanced meals of reasonable size for a fair price would be better.
reviews.title: Overrated

reviews.review_text:
A beautiful lunch. This meal has really stayed with me. A lovely neighbourhood restaurant setting, though don’t be fooled as the food is world-class. Warm service made the whole experience a real memory of our time in Lima. 

The ‘Choclo a la brasa’ starter was deceptively simple at first sight, but delivers a flavour punch that felt quintessentially Peruvian. And I don’t think I’ll ever forget the fish curry which was recommended by our waiter. We topped it all off with the Chocolate Rock for dessert. Ah the chocolate rock - I’ll give anything to have that again! 

We’ve recommended Merito to anyone who will listen ever since. It is a must-visit.

The meal is. thoughtful response to contemporary Latin dining,  For example, the cevice dish was the best we had in Lima.  The service was careful but not cloying. reviews.review_text: Omg food was soooo good, best we’ve had in Peru over three weeks. Cute, intimate setting and great service too. Love the corn starter (was like corn ribs) and have not stopped thinking about the choc rock dessert. Literally thinking of planning our flight out of Peru so we can go back throughLima for a night so I can eat the choc rock again. You should definitely eat here.
reviews.title: Eat here!!!

reviews.review_text:
We came to Lima to eat and Merito was our best meal.  Wonderful vibe, with small dining rooms upstairs and hovering above the kitchen.  Each dish was creative without trying too hard, tasted terrific, and really shined a light on the ingredients.  
In a city with a lot of high end restaurants, Merito stand out.

reviews.review_text: We went to dine there with our family of 5. We ordered 6 dishes.  They all arrived tapas style but I’m talking about TINY dishes.  The dishes also arrived one at a time making us hangrier and hangrier as each dish arrived.  Some of them dishes literally arrived with two pieces of food on it.  The internet clearly did NOT give any indication as to how small the dishes were.  We are literally sitting here still at the dinner table trying to find another restaurant to have an actual dinner at.   If you are here on a date don’t expect the girl to say yes to a second date, if you’re here with your family they will think you’re not very bright for it reading this review.  The food wasn’t even worth taking a picture of…if you don’t believe this review without the pictures of every plate then you deserve to overpay for what will end up being appetizers to whatever you eat once you leave here.

Buen ambiente, la comida buenisima  a

One of the best gastronomic experiences in Lima.
Although the street is rather noisy and not one of the cutest in the Barranco district, the place is definitely worth going.
You enter through the kitchen where you can see the cooks at work and go upstairs to find a nice minimalist deco restaurant.
We were a party of 5, ordered almost everything on the menu and shared all dishes among us.
Both cocktails and food are very creative and perfectly executed.
All fish dishes are wonderful, nicely spiced and perfectly cooked.
As for the desserts, the Flan is one of the best in my whole life, although it's more of a crème renversée than a proper Flan.

reviews.review_text:
I went to Mérito with the highest expectations as I had wanted to go since it opened and it had been highly recommended.  To begin, I will mention that the food was okay.  It was not great but it was not bad either.  It was nothing revolutionary.  Maybe revolutionary for Peru, since they don’t limit themselves to Peruvian flavors and Peruvian fusion and use Thai flavors and Venezuelan fusion but besides that, the food was  just ok.  

The real problem was the service and the attitude. 

The problem began when they took our drink orders.  First, they took more than 20 minutes to bring our cocktails even though we asked twice for them and the bar was nearly empty.  After they brought our drinks, they got one of the drinks wrong, and proceeded to argue with me about who was right.  After they left, they took another 15 minutes to bring the correct drink, at which point the dishes were already being served.  My drink actually arrived with our second dish. 

The timing of the dishes felt super rushed even though we told them that we were in no hurry. 

The next day when I checked the receipt (I didn’t check it carefully that night because we were rushed out because of the curfew, my bad), I noticed that I had been charged for the extra drink.   When I contacted the restaurant about it, of course they offered to refund the CC.  Obviously that has not happened yet.  

I understand that the pandemic has stressed the service industry particularly hard, which is why I still tipped a full 20% over the bill despite the bad service.  However, if Mérito is supposed to be one of the 50 Best Restaurants of Latin America, it should strive for very good service, especially as Peru re-opens it’s doors to tourists and welcomes them back.
reviews.title: Underwhelming

reviews.review_text: Su temática minimalista te da cierta comodidad y calidez. La decoración y los colores de su comida sobre platos confeccionados con el elemento tierra, resaltan a la vista y explotan en tu paladar. Lo amé tatalmente!!
reviews.title: Original y único en sabores y decoración.

reviews.review_text: Nice environment, good food, a pleasant experience. Overall a great choice to have a nice night in Barranco.
reviews.title: Great choice

reviews.review_text:
I recently went there for a dinner reservation. Arrived on time and started ordering some cocktails, all good. Received a very detailed explanation on the dishes which was really helpful and started ordering some things on the menu but asked not to bring them over still, as I was in no hurry at all (this was on a Saturday at 7 pm), and wanted to enjoy a few drinks before dinner. 

Accordingly, I ordered my second drink to the waitress and she nodded and walked away. I did noticed something weird in her attitude but decided to ignore her. A few minutes later came another waitress (a more “senior” one) and told me that they noticed I was asking for another drink but they wanted to start bringing over the food as they had another reservation coming over at 9:30 pm. It was only 7:45 pm. 

Lord knows it all went down from there. I should have just cancelled everything right then. Instead, I was polite enough and cancelled my second drink, and just let them bring the damn food over (flavors really good, some portions a bit small but ok, I get the concept). All in all, I was done by 8:30 pm (bill paid, no tip of course, as I do not condone this kind of behavior towards the customer).

If I were Merito’s owner, I would be really upset for having a couple of inexperienced people run my business without knowing that: 1. At a restaurant most profit margins come from alcoholic beverages (duh!) 2. They should avoid leaving an unattended table at a peak hour during the weekend for a whole 60 mins.

I felt absolutely mistreated and disrespected. I have been fortunate enough to dine at the world’s finest restaurants and I am no amateur, and this situation has never ever happened to me before, in places much more highly rated and with a much more higher status. Never coming back to this place, really disappointed. Avoid.
reviews.title: Totally disrespects the clients!

reviews.review_text: I had been picking my options to attend restaurants during the pandemic and this one looked like the one I can spend my few visits outside. We started with drinks, and we were visited constantly to pick the food. We pre-ordered to have more time for drinks until they came to say, you gotta order because we have a reservation at 9:30 pm. Of course, a couple of hours will be enough to have drinks and eat, but they were very desperate or looked like. We cut the last round of drinks, and ate, and left promptly at 8:30 pm, ONE HOUR BEFORE THEY NEEDED it to be cleared. I think that is really dumb since, although there is some other finance involved, if we kept drinking is better for them because there are always WAY BETTER margins on alcohol. I don't know what we event left them to serve the food. It was delicious, but the experience was already RUINED. Not coming back and definitely not recommending this place to locals or foreign visitors. You cannot do that to customers, you gotta manage your schedule and resources, and WE ALL KNOW there is a window of time, and WE AS CUSTOMERS always manage to keep our time to respect and share the space, no need to push that way.
reviews.title: Service, a big fail, good food--now it does not matter

reviews.review_text: The food was fantastic! We are a family of 4 including 2 teenagers, so I picked the a la carte option when making the reservation not wanting to lock my kids into the Nikkei experience with no choices. When we arrived, I asked if just I could do the Nikkei experience (the online reservation is all of nothing, not per person) and was told no, that it was only available by reservation. But, we were told we could do a 6 course meal, so 3 of us did that.  My husband had the short ribs that came with potatoes and rice and it was fantastic. The 6 course meal that my kids and I did proved to be a real experience and was great. Oddly enough, the last course was the entire short ribs meal my husband had, so that worked out that we got to have it as well since it was so good. I regularly found myself thinking that what I was eating tasted great, yet I had no idea what was in it and couldn't describe the flavor. It was just great! Service was also very good. Restaurant has no visible sign out front other than two plaques about it being rated in the top 50 restaurants in the world. We left stuffed and so happy we tried it.

reviews.review_text: Un lugar para disfrutar! El ambiente es muy nice (informal), la atención esmerada y cálida, y la comida buenísima!  Fuimos 4 comensales y decidimos compartir. De piqueo pedimos arepas (deli), tequeños (distintos, muy ricos y el guacamole de aplauso), unas conchitas a la brasa sabrosas, un pescado thai muy rico y un tartare con palta q para mi fue el piqueo ganador! Pedimos dos fondos, una panceta y una carrillera, ambos buenazos, por votación la carrillera fue la ganadora. Tip, pidan el arroz, buenazo. Postres, pedimos una crema volteada q era casi una crema catalana, deli y un postre de chocolate denominado  “la roca” q fue mi favorito porque soy chocolatera! Hay una cochera cerca pero se llena! Mejor ir en taxi. Vayan y disfruten.

reviews.review_text: Cocina fusión venezolana y peruana. Elaboración, sabor y presentación de los platos increíbles, por este nivel en otros restaurantes de Lima pagarías bastante más. El servicio correcto. Por poner una pega, la anfitriona no desempeña bien su papel, para como lo hace podría no estar allí y daría igual.

reviews.review_text:
Decidimos visitar Merito porque tenía muy buenas calificaciones en varias fuentes que revisamos, al llegar vimos que era un lugar pequeño y sólo había lugar en la barra.

Al sentarnos, se sintió lo acogedor del lugar, la proximidad con la cocina y con su personal nos agradó, lo primero que hicimos al pedir el menú y revisarlo fueron recomendaciones, de forma amable y servicial nos llevaron por todo el menú y el desglose de todos sus platillos y sugerencias.  No sabíamos que estábamos hablando con el chef  José Luis Saume

Gracias a esto, pedimos, la Quesadilla de Yuca, el Pulpo y la Pesca del día, todo excelente y muy rico.  Los sabores, términos y texturas de primera.  Para cerrar con broche de oro pedimos el Coco, el cual fue el gran ganador de la noche.

No me queda más que calificar con un 5 a este lugar, la verdad fue una excelente experiencia.  Espero algún día regresar a Perú y disfrutar de este lugar nuevamente.

PS. mi recomendación es que vayan a la barra y vivan la experiencia que se ve en la cocina.

Felicidades.
reviews.title: ¡El gran ganador del viaje!

reviews.review_text:
Small place which you barely notice from outside. 28 de Julio is noisy but once you are inside you dont notice.  Darkish wooden simple decor with a kitchen/counter eating downstairs and a few tables upstairs. Downstairs you get to watch the chefs.

The menu is small. 5 starters and 5 mains with a few deserts. There are links to Venezuela but the food is delicate and inventive, unlike anything you imagine from Vennie. Even the arepas are very light.
This is a place for sharing.  4 starters and two mains plus two deserts was enough for 4 people. Excellent yuca dish (dont think yuca, this is completely different). Delicious roasted corn with a dipping sauce. Mouth watering salad of "roots" and mushrooms. A chicken dish to die for. Excellent flan and chocolate deserts.  Good wine although not cheap. Overall about S./125 per head.

Lovely staff.  Only open evenings. If you dont book you can wait in bar nearby and they will call or come and fetch you when a table is free.
reviews.title: Wow! Brilliant Venezuelan fusion. Bravo los inmigrantes!

reviews.review_text: Loved the atmosphere. The quesadilla and the corn were next level. Best quesadilla I have ever had, even in Mexico. Really loved the drinks. The coconut dessert was one of the best ones I have ever had. Went back for lunch. Set menu. Really amazing too and incredibly reasonably priced.

reviews.review_text: Deliciosa comida, grandiosa atención y un concepto y experiencia diferente y encantadora!! Super recomendado, el lugar chiquito pero con encanto! Ve con tiempo porque se llena y a veces hay que esperar un poco :)

reviews.review_text: I loved everything I tried. The octopus sent me into food heaven. Make sure you come before they open if you want to avoid the line of diners eager to feast on their very delicious food.
reviews.title: Wonderful food

reviews.review_text:
Wow! Fusion food that features the best of Venezuela and Perú? 

Oh my goodness, how can you go wrong! The food is perfect. Great flavors. Spectacular presentation. Awesome service. Wonderful wine pours and bespoken cocktails. It’s the perfect package.

Okay, it’s a tiny spot with little room to stretch your elbows. But, that’s a near minor inconvenience. The food melds so delightfully to the foodie cultures of Perú and Venezuela - it gives both countries a clear path to their culinary expertise. 

I highly recommend this tiny Barranco spot for a lovely evening of gastronomic delights.
reviews.title: Wow!

reviews.review_text: Este lugar sabe a gloria. Es delicioso seguir el orden de su menú. El paso de los platos ligeros como el maíz asado con crema y llegar hasta la carne con costras de papas (y al medio varias opciones de setas, verduras y salsas) hacen de este sitio una gema de Barranco. Con un lugar acogedor para ir en pareja o con amigos. De los mejores lugares para visitar y comer de a pocos y en abundancia.
reviews.title: Volver una y otra vez

reviews.review_text:
Incríble el choclo con la salsa que me la hubiese llevado a toneladas: divina. Y obligatorio pedir el postre de La Roca. 
El pulpo excelente... bueno, todo.

reviews.review_text: This is one of the best restaurants that we have been to, and we have travelled all over the world ! Outward appearance is low key & chic. Excellent and knowledgeable service, and then the food arrives ... sensational !!! We had octopus & the spare rib, choc rock for dessert. A little expensive but well and truly worth the experience. Enjoy !
reviews.title: One of the best !

reviews.review_text: Pasamos por afuera y nos llamo la atención la hermosa barra que tiene. Entramos porque tenia opciones vegetarianas y normales ( dos menús ) . Todo esta delicioso y hermoso a la vista, desde la presentación de los platos hasta el delicioso postre ! Felicitaciones nos encanto!

reviews.review_text:
INCREDIBLE. 

There are no words to describe just how good Merito is. Every dish we tried was fantastic.
reviews.title: One of the best restaurants I’ve ever visited.

reviews.review_text:
Amazing and different Venezuelan and Peruvian food. The pork arepas are the best I’ve ever had. The hot vegan ceviche (mushrooms, corn, and other veggies) was delicious and so satisfying that we didn’t even miss the seafood. We also seriously considered licking the bowl. Don’t forget to save room for dessert. 

As a caution, they don’t have an English menu, since the restaurant is more of a local favorite than a tourist spot, and the staff do not speak a lot of English. However, the waiters are super helpful and patient and explained what the menu items were in slow Spanish to us. The prices are also very reasonable considering the high quality of the ingredients and the exquisite preparation.
reviews.title: Unique and Delicious Food

reviews.review_text: Extraordinario restaurant. Porciones pequeñas pero elaboradas con un cuidado estética y sabores únicos. Siéntese en la barra y pidan distintos platos para degustar y mirar como cocinan, un espectáculo y regalo para los sentidos.
reviews.title: Cada plato un poema

reviews.review_text:
La visita a este restaurante está más que justificada por su comida,que es exquisita. Es una pena que el servicio, bastante malo para un lugar como éste, no esté a la altura de la calidad de su carta.
Los cocktails son muy ricos también.
reviews.title: COMIDA EXQUISITA, SERVICIO MEDIOCRE

reviews.review_text: Y decir esto en Lima no es fácil; pero Mérito ha logrado una especie de emancipación de los sabores típicos de la comida fusión peruana, introduciendo elementos de una cocina latinoamericana más amplia, que ha resultado muy refrescante en la ya saturada oferta de restaurantes de la ciudad. El ambiente exquisito, la carta de vinos y piscos...buenísima. Hay que llegar temprano porque no se aceptan reservaciones, lo cual, es refrescante también.
reviews.title: El mejor restaurante de Lima.

reviews.review_text:
Fuimos con mi pareja a cenar a Mérito. Habíamos leído muy buenas referencias, las que realmente se hicieron realidad. La carta es clarísima, simple y exquisita. La preparación es delicada. Los sabores que consiguen con sus platos son maravillosos. 
Mi predilecto el Choclo a la brasa. MARAVILLOSO!!!
reviews.title: Lo sublime de lo simple

reviews.review_text: Merits is an amazing restaurant that is not overrun with tourists and visited by locals. We were tipped off to Merito by locals and loved our entire dining experience here. Since we had a late lunch we went with more starters and ended on dessert. The octopus, corn, gyoza and quesadilla were all phenomenal. We ended with getting the chocolate rock and chiromoya three ways. The rock alone from a presentation perspective is worth it. Highly recommend this place. We didn’t have any reservations we walked in early (Lima early) at 7:30 and were seated right away.
reviews.title: Excellent from Start to Finish

reviews.review_text: El Mérito has exceptional food! Although the food is pricey (between 20-60 soles per appetizer, $6-17) the experience is worth every sol! I sat at the bar which was a great way to see the food being prepared right in front of you. I was also able to chat with the 2 main chefs which is a rare opportunity in most restaurants of this calibre. They even let me hang around until closing to enjoy the atmosphere. I ordered the choclo and the pulpo (octopus) and both were amazing, resembling plates from the world famous Peruvian restaurant Central.  Highly recommend for a special night out!
reviews.title: Pricey but unique and tasty experience!

reviews.review_text: We had a really nice experience at Merito, which serves a fusion between venezuelan and peruvian food! The staff is friendly and informative and the dishes where interesting and delicious. We where 6 people, 3 of us vegetarian. This is a place where most dishes are ment to shared, so we shared among veggies and non veggies. The non vegetarians had the octopus, fish arepas and choclo. Veggies had choclo, green sallad, mushroom sallad and arepas. Everything was beautifully presented and delicious! The choclo dish was a real favourit for everyone, so simple but completely amazing! We also tried different kinds of non alcoholic infusions which where great, as well as really nice coffee. Would not miss a visit to this place when in Barranco!
reviews.title: Creative place with delicious food

reviews.review_text: We visited Merito as part of a “gastro  tour” with our amazing guide Gabriel. If you’re lucky enough to get a seat overlooking the kitchen, you’re in for an amazing experience... Nothing quite compares to watching Merito’s culinary  “artists” meticulously create an array dishes which are as delicious as they are beautiful. We tried their roasted corn, fish tartar, goat cheese quesadilla and grilled fish arepas - all served with unique and flavorful sauces of peppers and other herbs and vegetables. For dessert we had a baked chirimoya (tastes somewhat similar to apple or pear) with ice cream and shaved ice. Altogether a spectacular experience!!
reviews.title: Peruvian cuisine on steroids!

reviews.review_text: Fantastico Restaurante, todo encaja perfecto, el ambiente, servicio y los platos sin comentarios, una mezcla de sabor con los ingrendientes de la cocina andina, que  realmente te hace vivir esta experiencia a otro nivel. Un formato de restaurante distinto, donde estas cerca de los chefs, pocas mesas, con una carta a la medida que te permite probar más de un plato, por  no ser el tradicional plato de fondo ni la exquisitez de un menú degustacion. Excelente!!!
reviews.title: Una experiencia Gastronomica

reviews.review_text:
El local es acogedor pero muy pequeño, prácticamente rozas con la gente que esté en la mesa contigua lo que implica una pérdida total de intimidad y distensión.
Los cócteles relativamente buenos, pero el deseo de incentivar el consumo llega a ser agobiante, ya que interrumpen la charla a cada momento para prácticamente obligarte a consumir, lo que a mi parecer le quita categoría a la propuesta que pretenden difundir. Los platos son microscópicos con una forzada intención de adornarlos descuidando el contenido en pro de la forma. Me encantó la vajilla, pero al restaurante se va a comer y disfrutar y no a admirar la calidad de los vasos y los platos, no lo recomiendo ni volvería.
reviews.title: Sobrevalorado

reviews.review_text:
Delicioso. Buen ambiente, gran atención. La comida es toda una nueva experiencia por la cercanía del local y la profundidad de sus platos.

Ps. La roca de chocolate es un manjar.
reviews.title: Muy recomendable

reviews.review_text: Everything about Mérito is phenomenal.  The space is chic and quaint, the service is attentive and friendly, and the good is just amazing!  I highly recommend the lamb, octopus, and chocolate “rock”.  You will not be disappointed.
reviews.title: OMG - Amazing Dinner!!!

reviews.review_text: Hands down best food we have ever had. Great service, beautiful cozy space, and the food was insane. Absolutely insane.
reviews.title: WOW

reviews.review_text:
Excelente lugar, preocupados de mantener la armonía entre la decoración y sus platos. La atención excelente, cada plata que nos recomendaron fue increíble. Sin duda volvería.
Tienen que ir.
Buena relación precio - calidad
reviews.title: Sublime

reviews.review_text:
Si quieres deleitarte con alta gastronomía, usando ingredientes nativos y acompañada de deliciosos tragos y una atención DE LUJO, este es el lugar!
Salimos maravillados de los sabores y texturas y del amor que ponen en la preparación de los platos y en el servicio a los comensales.
Todo perfecto! 200% recomendado!
reviews.title: De primer nivel!

reviews.review_text: If you want to try something avant-gard you should definitely come over. Pretty much all the dishes I have tried have a unique or unexpected taste. I came here twice during my vacations in Lima.
reviews.title: Superb food ❤️

reviews.review_text: Excelente! El local en Barranco es chico pero muy acogedor, nos encantó la decoración y el ambiente. La atención muy buena también. De comer pedimos las conchas, los langostinos y el pulpo y todo espectacular! La combinación de ingredientes y sabores es extraordinaria
reviews.title: Muy Bueno!

reviews.review_text:
pocos lugares consiguen hacer de cada plato una obra de arte
lima se ha situado como capital gastronómica del continente del que alguna vez fue capital politica
viene gente de toda Sudamérica a practicar, aprender y crear culinariamente y no es sorpresa  que Juan Luis y Jose Luis  añadan este lugar a la oferta gastronómica limeña
reviews.title: really outstanding// verdaderamente excepcional

reviews.review_text:
The level of sophistication that this restaurant brings is amazing.  In a city that has a lot of great restaurants  ...this is a gem.  from the decor to the great service and the magic of making extraordinary food.
The chef is Venezuelan and he cooks with Peruvian ingredients.  there is a refinement and an innovation is the way the restaurant presents itself.

The decor is raw and dramatic and the lighting is also great
The food is hard to describe, because is an experience of flavors and presentation.

Great new favorite
reviews.title: Beyond good

reviews.review_text: Fui por una recomendación y no me defraudó. La entrada de pulpo es de lo mejor que comí en Lima al igual que los langostinos. Sabor a caribe. El fondo fue un pez diablo cocinado al carbón muy bueno y para cerrar, el mejor flan que probé en años. Súper recomendado!
reviews.title: Excelente!

reviews.review_text: This restaurant is a top culinary and social experience. The food is art - a fusion of flavors and presentation. The craft cocktails introduce and reward with new combinations. The wait staff, chefs and owners bring everything to life with the utmost attention and care. My wife and I can only name a handful of meals that rank equally well. We want to help their success. It is a small restaurant and hopefully will remain such to preserve the charm. We sat at the kitchen table (literally) and had a blast. Chevere chamos!!
reviews.title: This is why Lima has joined the international food scene!!

reviews.review_text: This small restaurant in the Barranco district of Lima is a real find. It had only been open for two months when we visited. It is small, rustic in a classy way and cozy. The chef and owners are two Venezuelans and create amazingly different dishes. Everything we had including the drinks was excellent.
reviews.title: Something different. Something excellent

reviews.review_text:
Una propuesta diferente y muy acertada, una fusión peruano venezolana e internacional muy bien lograda. Cuenta con una carta corta pero muy variada.
No dejen de probar el pescado a la parrilla y las mollejas,realmente destacables
Los precios son bastante razonables para lo que proponen
reviews.title: Destacado

reviews.review_text:
Fuimos tres amigos y pedimos todos los platos para compartir. Fueron tres platos magníficos.  Una chita (pescado de roca similar a la dorada de las costas españolas). Hecha al horno y acompañada de dos salsas con las que se untaba por dentro una arepa y luego se rellenaba con la carne de la chita.  Muy apropiado para compartir.  También pedimos unas conchas (vieiras) maceradas con limón y acompañadas con verduritas. Y por último unas mollejas de res deliciosas, eran mollejas de la zona de la garganta de la res. Las mollejas de la zona del corazón suelen ser mucho más grasientas.
Todo delicioso acompañado con un excelente vino local.
reviews.title: Una maravilla para los sentidos

reviews.review_text: Pequeño , sillas incomodas, raciones muy peque;as , la ración de pescado es escasa y el precio excesivamente caro ,compartiendo platos  para dos personas 203 soles .La chirimoya a la parrilla incomestible esa mezcla no tiene recorrido.
reviews.title: Muy mala relacion cantidad precio.

reviews.review_text:
Para decir verdad... este sitio no merece estar en el puesto 475... Para mí parecer debería estar dentro de los top 10 de Lima... tienen tanto... espacio super acogedor, personal atento y amable, y la comida... Ni hablar, deliciosa, novedosa, sabores y texturas increíbles.

Un rincón en Barranco que sin duda alguna te falta espacio para comer todo Lo que allí tienen, desde la bebida hasta el Postre. Una vez visitado es casi obligado volver para seguir deleitandose. Los precios son bastante razonable.

Muchas gracias a Priscila que nos atendió y nos hizo sentir como en casa.. 

A los chef, sólo me queda decirles que sigan explotando y desarrollando el potencial que tienen en las manos, realmente lo hacen muy bien. Ánimo que estoy segura estarán en ese top 10 que considero... Lo tienen todo!!!
reviews.title: Descubrimiento increíble... Barranco

reviews.review_text:
Realmente difícil saber que no decir.

Vivimos en Lima, y afortunadamente hemos podido estar en los principales restaurantes se hay en este país, por lo que se bien de lo que escribire en este comentario.

Local acogedor, original decoración, excelente atención, increíble presentación de los platos, muy buena calidad de los productos, innovación de sabores, lo mejor es que se dejen llevar por las recomendaciones, no les defraudarán.

Nosotros pedimos tres entrantes (almejas, pulpo y mollejas) y un plato de fondo (cabrito) recomendando todo.

Los postres igualmente recomendables, nosotros pedimos el flan (algo tan "sencillo" ha sido llevado a otro nivel) y la "roca" de chocolate... mejor pruebenlo!! 

Y algo que hemos valorado mucho ha sido el asesoramiento de Priscilla, sincero y siempre con una sonrisa, haciendo de nuestro paso por este restaurante sea recordado por hacernos sentir como en casa.

A José y Jorge (los chefs) decirles que cuando se pone todo en el trabajo, y en este caso se une con una excelente materia prima y ganas de innovar, el resultado es increíble. 

Felicitaciones!! Sigan así!!

Sinceramente GRACIAS!!!
reviews.title: Increíblemente bueno!

reviews.review_text:
Located at the trendy barranco area merito offers a very sophisticated experience that appears simple. 

In line with the famous Peruvian culinary experience it offers surprising presentations for very interesting dishes. 

It should definitively be on your list when you visit barranco.
reviews.title: True elegance is simple

reviews.review_text: I visited Merito with my girlfriend and it has been an amazing discover.  The Chefs are using amazing techniques of cooking, using Peruvian and Venezuelan flavours. Everything in there has sense,  the design, the chairs, the cutlery,  the menu and the floor staff is really informed and polite to answer at every question. The octopus and the sweetbreads were sensational,  cooked at the perfection and plated with style...I really loved it and highly recommended. I cannot give 5 stars just because I received my starter in a different timing of my girlfriend ( we didn't want to share the starters,  but just the main course) so I had to wait quite long time for my first bite, a bit annoying. Probably just a misunderstanding, because the level of the restaurant is very high.
reviews.title: Techniques and great flavours

reviews.review_text:
Excelente restaurante en Barranco, el lugar es pequeño pero muy acogedor, la atención es de primera y la comida espectacular!
Pedimos varias entradas para compartir,  todas muy buenas, de fondo el pescado (en este caso Fortuno), insuperable y la Panceta exquisita. Los postres cada uno mejor que el otro, empezando por la Roca de Chocolate, el Flan y la deliciosa Chirimoya.
En general todo de primera, pero de PRIMERA!
Del 1 al 10 le pondría 10 puntos!
reviews.title: "Muy buenoooooo"

reviews.review_text: My wife, daughter and and I were recommended by a Parisian couple to try this spot- they raved about it. Now we know why, though the presentation was spectacular, the combination of tastes on each dish was superlative. The octopus dish was the best I’ve ever had. Every dish we had was outstanding. As we were seating by the bar, watching the creative chefs at work was a treat! This made for a fabulous last nice in Lima- worth the trip to Baranco.
reviews.title: Exceptional, creative flavours!!

reviews.review_text: This is my second visit to Merito and it did not disappoint. Fabulous dishes with fresh ingredients.  Love the way they prepare the Tiradito and the baked fish.  The fried yuccas and the choclo dish are a great way to get started.
reviews.title: Tinny eatery packing  a huge punch

reviews.review_text: I visited Merito as part of a girls’ night out and really enjoyed the Peruvian- Venezuelan food. The menu is very small but includes various vegetarian options so that probably won me over. As a group of 4, we tried most things on the menu and all dishes were enjoyed. The wine list is also tiny but I was happy with the Prosecco on hand. My only complaint is that the location is small and they don’t take bookings nor do they have a waiting area, which meant we had to wait more than an hour for a table at another location. Fortunately it’s a couple of doors up from Barra 55 so that’s a great option for a pre-dinner drink or two as you wait, and you can send someone from your party to keep checking on the table, as Merito will not call you when your table is ready nor accept phone calls from you to check. Were Merito to change their policy on bookings or phone calls I would definitely score them higher as I loved the place regardless of the inconvenience they caused my group. Please do check them out, but go when you’re relaxed and ready to wait!
reviews.title: Great for small groups

reviews.review_text: Nice surprise! It’s not on any list of best gastronomy in Lima but it should be. The service was impeccable and the menu was varied and with innovative and delicious options. There was no disappointment at all. We strongly recommend!
reviews.title: Wonderful experience!

reviews.review_text: La comida es deliciosa. Definitivamente un lugar para recomendar a todo al que le guste comer bien. El descubrimiento del menú: las mollejas y choclo, las pedí por sugerencia de los chefs y quedé encantada. Todo lo que probé estuvo fantástico. Volveré!
reviews.title: Maravilloso descubrimiento

reviews.review_text:
Una carta pequeña pero acertada. Cocina abierta, platos tratados a nivel quirúrgico. Ayer fuimos por tercera vez, comimos el arroz meloso de langostinos, ensalada de setas, choclo con queso y dos de los tres postres de la carta; el mejor flan que he comido en mi vida y la chirimoya a la parrilla. 
Salimos muy satisfechos, de nuevo diciendo que nos parece el mejor restaurante de Lima.
reviews.title: Otra dimensión

reviews.review_text: We went to Merito as part of a Barranco Food Tour. Everything we had was wonderful, but the octopus dish was the stand-out...tender and succulent! We also really liked the passionfruit Pisco sours. We would highly recommend this restaurant.
reviews.title: The best octopus we've ever had in our lives!

reviews.review_text: Merito Restaurant in Barranco (Lima) is a true hole in the wall that hits you with a powerful savory punch with their assortment of dishes.  Venezuelan chefs Juan Luis Martínez y José Luis Saumeo are dealing with a very sophisticated culinary crowd in Lima and they deliver.  Juan Luis worked for two years as a chef at La Central Restaurant in Lima which is considered one of the top 10 restaurants in the word and it shows.  The service, the presentation and the quality of the cuisine are a reflection of a highly trained team. The superb quality of culinary options in Lima keeps growing. No surprise that Peru for the 7th year in the row is considered the best culinary destination in the world.
reviews.title: A United Nations of Savory

reviews.review_text: Excelente fusión peruana/venezolana con platos realmente BUENOS. Carta pequeña pero con combinaciones sorprendentes. Pedimos las conchas con papas y el pulpo, súper sabroso. De segundo el cabrito (espectacular, lo mejor para mi) y las arepas con panceta. Todo muy bien logrado y con una atención de primera. Como bebidas hay vino (copa y botella), cocktails (el de lulo con pisco estaba delicioso), cervezas y gaseosas. Definitivamente voy a volver a probar lo que me faltó.
reviews.title: Súper RECOMENDADO!!

reviews.review_text:
visitamos este lugar buscando una probada de la cocina contemporánea en lima  , este acogedor lugar nos preparo unos platos deliciosos y únicos. Tienen muy buenas opciones vegetarianas y el precio me pareció muy justo . 
Probamos las conchas con papa volada, ensalada de setas(recomendadisima ) el choclo a la brasa y de postre el flan ( final perfecto) . Recomiendo sentarse  en la barra del primer piso y ver toda la acción de la cocina .
reviews.title: D E L I C I O S O !

reviews.review_text:
El restaurante está ubicado en un local muy pequeño pero con su particular encanto en Barranco. La comida sobresaliente, sabores y presentaciones muy buenos. Me fascinaron las arepas, preparadas con otra técnica, pero con un sabor muy particular y rico. El ceviche, las yucas, y en general todos los platos que probamos nos sorprendieron muy gratamente. 
Sin duda voy a regresar, un gran descubrimiento en el panorama limeño.
reviews.title: Fusión Peruano-Venezolana exquisita!

reviews.review_text:
Headed by a Sous chef from Central (just 2 blocks away), this was mind blowing. Perhaps the best Octopus I've had in 2 years. I'm not quite sure how they cooked it so that the outside was gelatinous, the inside firm and suckers charred and crispy, all at the same time. Magnificent.

The panceta and arepas asado reminded me of Chinese pork buns but...distinctly Peruvian. Another fantastic riff on classic flavor profiles bound to delight. 

This is the perfect place for those who want the ingenuity and flavor packed profile of Central but could not score a reservation or do not wish to ingest a 12 course, 3 hour long meal.
reviews.title: For those who want Central with no reservations

reviews.review_text: If you're not too fussed about your surroundings, love tasty, different and well presented food, and prefer not to spend a fortune then head for Merito. Slightly odd location a block and a bit from the main Barranco piazza, there are a few stools at the bar where dishes are prepared downstairs and some more seating with comfortable tables and benches/chairs upstairs (the adobe bricks give that area a slightly distressed look offset by the well chosen furnishings). The menu is short but very appetising with a mixture of Peruvian and Venezuelan elements (roast choclo/corn on one side, arepas on the other with fried yuca in between), and all the starters and mains we tried had interesting vegetables/sauces. There wasn't a dud among our choices and some outstanding offerings including the scallop/squid, the roast fish (cabrillo), and the sepas with (among other things) black radishes. Despite being replete all dishes were wiped clean and there was still room to try the a couple of the desserts (there are only three) with the roca de chocolate being the winner by a head. Apart from regular Pilsen, two artesan beers (one wheat based but clear) are available as well as half a dozen wines. The coffee is excellent if you like it strong. Service is first rate - knowledgeable, friendly and efficient. And the prices ? Extremely good value for food this interesting and of this quality (90 soles per head excluding service but including an alcoholic beer each). Go now before the place gets too popular !
reviews.title: this really is the business

reviews.review_text: Fui sorprendido, literalmente, con la propuesta de estos cocineros de Venezuela. Una mezcla de sabores que deleita y agasaja los sentidos. Les recomiendo las mollejas, el cabrito, arepas con mantequillas, lleno de sensaciones que los volverán locos!!
reviews.title: Cena en Barranco

reviews.review_text: Excelente restayrante, con una barra muy buena, donde te sentas y ves como emplatan los cocineros. Sabores muy marcados y un servicio muy bueno
reviews.title: Excelente lugar!

reviews.review_text:
Located at the back of plaza Barranco,
A really nice peruvian/Venazuela restaurant.
They really took the qualities from Central and put their on style in to this place.
Hope many people find way to Mérito, I will be there soon again.
reviews.title: new gem restaurant
